title: Before planning: seven facts to gather
objectives: Gather the seven facts and say why each matters.
Ask the seven questions in plain words.
body_md:
A withdrawal plan starts from the client's spending, not from the corpus.

| Fact | Question to ask | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly need | “What do you spend each month, essentials vs extras?” | Sets the withdrawal amount; essentials need the most secure source |
| Other income | “Any pension, rent, annuity, interest or part-time income?” | Reduces what the portfolio must provide |
| Big expenses ahead | “Any planned costs: travel, a child's wedding, a car, home repairs?” | Plan these separately so they don't derail the SWP |
| Health and insurance | “Do you have health cover for yourself and your spouse?” | Medical costs are the biggest threat to a retirement corpus |
| Horizon | “How many years should this money last, including for your spouse?” | Longer horizons need a lower withdrawal rate |
| Whole corpus | “What do you hold across EPF, PPF, FDs, SCSS, funds and property?” | Shows the true withdrawal rate and asset mix |
| Comfort with risk | “How would you feel if your portfolio fell 20% in your first year?” | Sets the size of the safety buffer |
example: Ask: “What do you spend each month, essentials vs extras?” “Any pension, rent, annuity, interest or part-time income?” “How many years should this money last, including for your spouse?”
say: A withdrawal plan starts from spending, not from the corpus.
Essentials need the most secure source.
never: Ignore health cover and other income.

check.q: Which is the biggest threat to many retirement corpuses?
check.why: Medical costs without health cover. Check health cover.

check.q: What does a withdrawal plan start from?
o: The client's spending, not the corpus
check.why: A withdrawal plan starts from the client's spending, not from the corpus.

check.q: Why ask about health and insurance?
o: Medical costs are the biggest threat to a retirement corpus
check.why: Health and insurance: medical costs are the biggest threat to a retirement corpus.
